The use of artificial intelligence in education is becoming an increasing priority. The purpose of this study was to examine academics' views on the implications of artificial intelligence (AI)-supported verbal intelligence games for open and confirmatory inquiry, problem-solving, and scientific reasoning skills in education. The study group consisted of 13 academics. Convenience sampling was employed to select the participants. A phenomenological research design, one of the qualitative research methods, was adopted in this study. Qualitative data were collected through a semi-structured interview form. The collected qualitative data were analyzed using the inductive content analysis method. The findings revealed that the participants held positive views regarding AI-supported verbal intelligence games. Furthermore, the participants stated that AI-supported verbal intelligence games had positive implications for open and confirmatory inquiry, problem-solving, scientific reasoning, and reasoning skills in education. Based on these findings, recommendations were made for educators and policymakers.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.55549/jeseh.926\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 10, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5040/9798400660580.ch-004\", \"title\": [\"Open: Invitation to inquiry, Open minds, Stimulate curiosity\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5040/9798400660580.ch-004\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2012]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5771/9781607096368-29\", \"title\": [\"Chapter 2.
